ISSUE:0023 (medium; not started, hv quiesced for the move and travel): the first `molt upgrade` after a pull that changes lib/ runs the old library against the new liberators. bin/molt sources lib/ at start, cmd_upgrade re-sources only constants.sh after _upgrade_pull_repos, and liberator_load sources the pulled liberators, so with WP02 merged the first upgrade on every sleeve ends `2 liberator(s) failed` and renders no home; the second run works. Fix in cmd_upgrade's full path: record the framework HEAD before _upgrade_pull_repos; when it changed and the run is not a dry run, say so on one line and re-exec `"$MOLT_ROOT/bin/molt" upgrade` with an option that skips the pull (eg --no-pull), carrying the resleeve flags through, so the hooks and the resleeve run on the new code. Re-sourcing lib/*.sh in place is not enough: the old bin/molt does not know which new library files to source. One test: a scratch framework repo whose pull brings a liberator calling a function only the pulled lib/ defines; assert the liberator ran on the new code. Both bashes. Branch issue-0023 from main in a worktree, head to vc. Should land before rhadamanth moves; WP04's runbook works around it meanwhile (A1: `molt upgrade --self`, then `molt upgrade`). messages.body: cc: WP06 Molt head for your guide is st0006-wp06 1720f99 (vc merges). Sidecar: <managed>/managed-settings.d/molt-sysadm.json.molt-rendered, root 644, written first; lines 'rendered <date> from <floor.json>', 'digest <sha256>', 'output <sha256>'. Scope: the sleeve's molt.toml enables a sysadm agent AND its vars.sh declares MOLT_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. Doctor 14: '✓ in place: <target>'; '✓ none needed; <target> is not molt's, and is left'; '✓ none needed, and none of molt's here'; '⚠' followed by one of: '<target> is missing', '<target> is not <floor.json>', '<target> was not written by molt, which leaves it', '<target> is molt's, and this sleeve carries no floor: it has no enabled sysadm agent, or declares no MOLT_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR', '<target> could not be compared with <floor.json>', 'MOLT_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR could not be read: ...'. Install faults, each prefixed 'agents: managed floor: ': 'a sysadm agent needs its managed floor, and there is no <floor.json>, so nothing was written'; '<floor.json> is not one object holding only permissions.deny, a list of strings, so nothing was written'; '<target> was not written by molt, which leaves it, so the floor is not in place'; 'sudo is not installed, so <target> was not written'; 'sudo could not install <target>'. On success: 'Rendered: <floor.json> -> <target>'; on removal: 'Removed the managed floor: <target>'. molt agent config <host>-sysadm lists the drop-in under managed, and its two rules tagged managed.
